population.definition: Harare Province (not the city alone), de facto count of people who spent census night 20 April 2022 in the province; preliminary results. A city-only figure was not found in a readable source.

source.title: 2022 Population and Housing Census: Preliminary Report on Population Figures
source.author: Taguma Mahonde, Director-General (preface)
source.quote: Harare Province had 2,427,209 persons.

facts.claim: The first British settlement on the site was named Fort Salisbury after the 3rd Marquess of Salisbury; the BSAC pioneer column reached the area in September 1890.

source.title: Harare, Zimbabwe (Research Starters)
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: The first British settlement there was named Fort Salisbury after the 3rd Marquess of Salisbury.

facts.claim: On the anniversary of independence in 1982 (18 April) Salisbury was renamed Harare, after the Shona chief Neharawa (SAHO spelling).

source.title: Capital City of Zimbabwe is renamed
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: Zimbabwe renamed its capital city Harare, after the Shona chief Neharawa.

facts.claim: EBSCO gives the chief's name as Haarare and the renaming year as 1982; sources spell the chief's name differently.

source.title: Harare, Zimbabwe (Research Starters)
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: The word Harare was borrowed from the name of the local Shona tribal chief Haarare.

source.quote: before the nation gained independence in 1980 as the Republic of Zimbabwe, retaining Salisbury as its capital.

places.name: Mbare Musika
places.what: Mbare Musika is a fresh produce market in the Mbare area of Harare. A 2023 University of Pretoria thesis traces it from 1930 and credits African farmers and traders, especially women, with building it.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: Built by African farmers and traders, especially women

source.title: An actor oriented history of Mbare Musika fresh produce market, Zimbabwe 1930-2019
source.author: Stephen Hahlani
source.quote: Mbare Musika was built through the efforts of African farmers and traders, especially women

facts.label: Municipal recognition
facts.value: Salisbury Municipality recognised African markets in the 1940s

source.title: An actor oriented history of Mbare Musika fresh produce market, Zimbabwe 1930-2019
source.author: Stephen Hahlani
source.quote: the Salisbury Municipality recognised African markets in the 1940s

source.title: An actor oriented history of Mbare Musika fresh produce market, Zimbabwe 1930-2019
source.author: Stephen Hahlani
source.quote: Mbare Musika was expanded after the independence of Zimbabwe in 1980.

source.title: An actor oriented history of Mbare Musika fresh produce market, Zimbabwe 1930-2019
source.author: Stephen Hahlani
source.quote: The market remains an important source of food in Harare.

places.name: Chapungu Sculpture Park
places.what: Chapungu is a 20-acre sculpture park on the outskirts of Harare showing Zimbabwean stone sculpture, also called Shona sculpture. It began as a small gallery in the city and its founder is named as Roy Guthrie.

source.title: About Us | Chapungu
source.quote: the 20 acre sculpture park in the outskirts of Harare

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Began as a small gallery in Harare

source.title: About Us | Chapungu
source.quote: a small gallery in the capital city, Harare

facts.label: Collection claim (self-described)
facts.value: Park says it holds the most important permanent collection of this work

source.title: About Us | Chapungu
source.quote: the most important permanent collection of this work in existence through Chapungu

places.name: National Heroes' Acre
places.what: National Heroes' Acre is a state shrine and burial ground near Harare. Scholarship describes it as used by ZANU-PF to shape national identity.

facts.label: Role (academic view)
facts.value: Used for national identity through state rituals

source.title: Making heroes, (un)making the nation?: ZANU-PF's imaginations of the Heroes Acre, heroes and construction of identity in Zimbabwe from 2000-
source.author: Shepherd Mpofu
source.quote: acts as a tool for national identity and its symbolic maintenance through state presided rituals.

facts.label: Political critique (attributed to Mpofu, 2017)
facts.value: Author argues elite use excludes public participation

source.title: Making heroes, (un)making the nation?
source.author: Shepherd Mpofu
source.quote: excludes democratic public participation.
